If you've spent any time reading skincare labels lately, you've probably seen Niacinamide listed near the top. It's not a trend ingredient — it's a form of Vitamin B3 that's been studied for decades, and for good reason.

What Niacinamide Actually Does

Niacinamide supports the skin's natural barrier, helps even out the look of skin tone, and works well alongside almost every other active ingredient — which is part of why it's so widely used. Unlike stronger actives that can be harsh on sensitive skin, Niacinamide tends to be well tolerated by most skin types, including oily, combination, and acne-prone skin.

What to Expect

Skincare results take time and consistency — there's no honest shortcut here. With regular use, many people notice their skin looking calmer, more even, and less prone to excess shine over several weeks of consistent use.

How We Use It

In our face serum, Niacinamide is formulated at a supportive concentration alongside complementary botanicals, so it works with your skin rather than overwhelming it. We name it on the label because we believe you should always know exactly what you're putting on your skin.

Making It Part of Your Routine

A simple way to start: cleanse, apply a few drops of serum to damp skin, follow with a moisturizer, and always finish your morning routine with sunscreen. Small, consistent steps tend to outperform complicated ten-step routines.

Aloe Vera Gel Benefits for Skin and Hair: Why It Belongs in Your Daily Routine
blogs.content:
What Is Aloe Vera?

Aloe Vera has been trusted for centuries to soothe, hydrate, and protect skin. Today it remains one of the most versatile skincare ingredients — its gel contains polysaccharides, vitamins C & E, and anti-inflammatory compounds that support skin health across all types. It is not merely a sunburn remedy; that's a fraction of what it does.


Benefits of Aloe Vera for Skin

Hydration Without Greasiness

Aloe is a humectant — it draws moisture to the skin and holds it there without a greasy residue, making it ideal for oily, combination, and acne-prone skin that needs hydration without weight.

Calms and Soothes

Its anti-inflammatory properties reduce redness and soothe skin after sun, wind, or environmental exposure — which is why it works so reliably as after-sun care.

Supports the Skin Barrier

Polysaccharides form a light protective layer on the skin's surface. A stronger barrier means less reactivity, better moisture retention, and more comfortable skin day to day.

Benefits of Aloe Vera for Hair

On the scalp, Aloe supports moisture balance and clears excess sebum without stripping natural oils. On hair strands, its amino acids smooth the cuticle, reduce frizz, and improve manageability with regular use.

Who Should Use It?

•     Oily or acne-prone skin needing hydration without clogged pores

•     Dry or sensitive skin that reacts to heavier creams

•     Dry or itchy scalp, or frizzy, difficult-to-manage hair

•     Anyone wanting one multi-use product for face, body, and hair

 Setting Realistic Expectations

Aloe Vera works by supporting the skin's natural environment. Expect calmer, better-balanced skin over 4–6 weeks of consistent daily use — meaningful improvements that build quietly over time.

Consistency with a gentle ingredient almost always outperforms intensity with an aggressive one.


Why Nezal Uses Aloe Vera

•     Multi-purpose hydration — face, body, and scalp in one product

•     Lightweight and non-greasy — suitable even for oily skin

•     Supports the skin barrier while other actives do their work

•     Suitable for all skin types with no known common contraindications

•     Named plainly on the label: Aloe Barbadensis Leaf Extract — no euphemisms

 

How to Use Aloe Vera Gel

Face: Apply a small amount to slightly damp skin after cleansing. Use alone as a lightweight moisturiser or under a richer cream.

Body: Apply after showering while skin is still slightly damp. Especially effective on sun-exposed areas and dry patches.

Scalp: Massage into the scalp 30 minutes before shampooing as a pre-wash treatment.

Hair ends: Work a small amount through mid-lengths and ends as a lightweight frizz-control leave-in.

After sun: Apply a generous layer to all sun-exposed areas immediately after exposure. Refrigerate beforehand for extra cooling relief.

Biggest mistake: using too much. A thin, even layer does the job — more is not more.

 

Frequently Asked Questions

Can Aloe Vera Gel be used daily?

Yes. It is gentle enough for twice-daily use on all skin types. Apply to clean skin for lightweight hydration and soothing care.

Can it help dry skin?

Yes, though very dry skin may benefit from layering Aloe under a richer moisturiser. Aloe draws moisture in; a heavier cream seals it.

Can it be used on hair?

Yes — as a pre-shampoo scalp treatment or a lightweight leave-in on hair ends. Start with a small amount and adjust.

Can it be used overnight?

Yes. A thin layer before sleep supports skin recovery without clogging pores — many oily skin types use it as a lighter alternative to night creams.

Is it good for acne-prone skin?

Yes. It is non-comedogenic, anti-inflammatory, and provides hydration without heaviness — one of the most acne-friendly options available.

Most mass-produced soaps remove the Glycerin that forms naturally during soap-making and sell it separately — the result is a bar that strips the skin. Our Designer Soaps keep it in.

If your skin feels tight after washing, your soap has had its glycerin removed.

Benefits for Skin

Comfort After Every Wash

Glycerin draws moisture during washing; Shea Butter seals it in after rinsing. Skin feels comfortable immediately — no tightness, no dryness.

Suitable for Sensitive Skin

Shea Butter's fatty acids closely mimic the skin's natural lipids, counteracting the stripping effect of cleansing without over-conditioning or clogging pores.

Reduces Reliance on Body Moisturiser

Many people find they need less body lotion after switching — the soap stops actively removing natural moisture with every wash.

Who Should Use It?

•     Dry or very dry skin needing moisture even from the cleansing step

•     Sensitive skin that reacts to fragrance-heavy or sulphate-rich products

•     Anyone looking to simplify their daily bath routine

•     Those wanting a premium, beautifully crafted gifting option

 Setting Realistic Expectations

A soap is a rinse-off product — its job is to cleanse. What a well-formulated bar adds is skin that feels comfortable after every wash. That difference is felt every single day.

Why Nezal Uses Shea Butter and Glycerin

•     Glycerin retained in every bar — not removed commercially

•     Shea Butter's fatty acids survive the rinse for post-wash conditioning

•     Aesthetic craftsmanship — design, weight, and fragrance are intentional

Lather: Work the bar into a lather in your palms before applying — distributes evenly and extends bar life.

Apply: Use gentle circular motions on damp skin. No scrubbing required.

Store: Keep on a well-drained soap dish. A bar sitting in water dissolves in half the time — dry storage gives 4–6 weeks per bar.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Shea Butter soap good for oily skin?

Yes. It cleanses without stripping natural oils, which can help oily skin regulate sebum production — it will not make oily skin greasier.

Can Glycerin soap be used on the face?

Yes. Our formula is non-comedogenic and gentle enough for daily facial use on most skin types.

How long does a bar last?

Stored on a dry soap dish, a 100–120g bar lasts 4–6 weeks with daily use.

Why does premium soap cost more?

Because the ingredients — retained Glycerin, Shea Butter — cost more than stripped commercial soap bases. The difference shows in how your skin feels after every wash.

blogs.title: pH Balanced Intimate Wash: Why Lactic Acid and Tea Tree Make All the Difference
blogs.content:
What Is pH Balanced Intimate Wash?

The intimate area maintains a naturally acidic pH of 3.8–4.5. Regular soaps (pH 8–10) are far too alkaline — they disrupt this natural environment every time they are used. A pH-balanced intimate wash, formulated with Lactic Acid and cleansed with Tea Tree Oil, keeps the product in the correct range so it supports rather than disturbs the body's own defences.

pH balance in intimate care is not a marketing claim — without it, a product can cause the very discomfort it claims to prevent.

Key Ingredients

Lactic Acid

An AHA that acts as a gentle exfoliant and pH regulator, keeping the wash in the 3.8–4.5 range the intimate area needs.

Tea Tree Oil

A well-researched cleansing ingredient used at a concentration appropriate for sensitive intimate tissue — chosen for its cleansing action, not its fragrance.

Benefits

Daily Comfort — All Genders

People switching from soap to a pH-balanced wash typically notice less dryness and irritation within 2–3 weeks. The intimate area's self-regulating properties are supported, not disrupted.

Why Unisex?

The pH requirement for intimate hygiene is the same regardless of gender. Gendering this product would be a marketing decision, not a formulation one. We chose not to make it.

Who Should Use It?

•     Anyone currently using soap or body wash for intimate cleansing

•     People experiencing dryness or mild irritation in the intimate area

•     All genders — the pH science applies equally to everyone

Why Nezal Made This Unisex

•     pH requirements are identical for all genders — no scientific basis for separation

•     Lactic Acid ensures correct formulation pH, not just correct labelling

•     Tea Tree Oil at a clinically appropriate concentration — not a headline ingredient

•     Formulated for once-daily use — designed to support, not overwhelm

 How to Use

Amount: A 50-paise coin-sized amount — the product is more concentrated than it appears.

Apply: To the external intimate area only during bathing. Never for internal use.

Frequency: Once daily. Over-washing can itself disrupt the natural balance you are supporting.

Less is genuinely more — small amount, once a day, consistently.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is intimate wash necessary if I use soap?

Yes. Soap's pH of 8–10 disrupts the intimate area's natural 3.8–4.5 pH every time. A pH-balanced wash is the correct product for this area.

Can men use intimate wash?

Yes — specifically formulated Unisex. The pH requirement applies equally to all genders.

How much should I use?

A 50-paise coin-sized amount is sufficient. More does not increase benefit.

Can it be used daily?

Yes — once daily during bathing. More than once daily is unnecessary and may cause disruption.

blogs.title: Hydrating Shower Gel: How Coconut-Derived Cleansers and Vitamin E Change Your Daily Shower
blogs.content:
What Is Moisturising Shower Gel?

A moisturising shower gel replaces harsh sulphate-based surfactants with gentler coconut-derived alternatives, and adds Vitamin E as a conditioning agent that survives the rinse. The result is a shower gel that cleans thoroughly but leaves skin feeling comfortable rather than tight and dry.

Key Ingredients

Coconut-Derived Cleansers

Surfactants derived from coconut oil (such as Cocamidopropyl Betaine) produce a rich, creamy lather without the aggressive moisture-stripping associated with SLS and SLES found in most mass-market products.

Vitamin E (Tocopherol)

A fat-soluble antioxidant that is one of the few actives that meaningfully survives rinse-off, leaving a light conditioning film on the skin's surface to support hydration post-shower.

Benefits

No Post-Shower Tightness

The tight, dry feeling after showering is not a sign of cleanliness — it signals a stripped moisture barrier. Coconut-derived surfactants clean without causing it.

Less Reliance on Body Moisturiser

With consistent use, many people need less lotion after switching — the gel stops removing what the skin naturally produces with every wash.

Think of a good shower gel as one that stops taking something away from your skin.

Who Should Use It?

•     Dry or sensitive skin experiencing tightness after every shower

•     Anyone who showers frequently and wants a gentle daily formula

•     Those wanting a luxury sensory experience without compromising skin health

Why Nezal Chose These Ingredients

•     Coconut-derived surfactants produce luxury lather without post-shower dryness

•     Vitamin E provides proven conditioning residue — not a label claim

•     Sulphate-free formulation safe for daily use

•     Fragrance designed to be present but never overpowering — a shower is a ritual

 How to Use

Apply: To thoroughly wet skin — surfactants need water to activate properly.

Lather: Use a loofah or shower puff for better distribution, more lather, and less product used.

Rinse: Until water runs completely clear — residue on skin prevents Vitamin E from conditioning effectively.

Follow: With body moisturiser on damp skin within 2–3 minutes for best absorption.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why does my current shower gel make skin feel tight?

Almost certainly SLS or SLES — aggressive sulphate surfactants that strip the skin's natural moisture. Switching to a coconut-derived formula resolves this from the first use.

Can shower gel be used daily?

Yes — our formula is specifically designed for daily use without cumulative drying effects.

Is Vitamin E effective in a rinse-off product?

Yes — it is one of the few actives that provides meaningful conditioning benefit after rinsing. You will feel the difference.

Does it replace body moisturiser?

Not completely, but many people need significantly less. Apply moisturiser on damp post-shower skin for best results.

•     Salicylic Acid is one of the only actives that genuinely earns its place in a rinse-off formula for oily skin

•     Green Tea counters sensitisation — the formula cleanses deep without causing dryness

•     Foaming format delivers active ingredients evenly across the face in each use

•     Concentration calibrated for daily rinse-off use — not a leave-on strength

 How to Use — Step by Step

Water: Dampen face with lukewarm water — never hot, which worsens redness and damages the barrier.

Lather: Work a small amount into foam on damp hands. Apply to face in circular motions for 30–60 seconds — contact time matters for BHA.

Rinse: With cool water to help tighten pores. Pat dry immediately.

Follow: With your serum or Aloe Vera Gel on slightly damp skin for best absorption.

Frequency: Twice daily for oily skin; once daily (evening) for combination skin.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can Salicylic Acid face wash be used daily?

Yes for oily and acne-prone skin. If you notice dryness, switch to once daily in the evening and monitor your skin's response.

How long before I see results?

Reduced shine is immediate. Visible improvement in congestion and blemishes takes 4–8 weeks of consistent twice-daily use.

Is it suitable for dry skin?

It's designed for oily and combination skin. Dry skin types can use it once or twice weekly as a deeper-cleansing treatment.

Can Green Tea extract be combined with other actives?

Yes — one of the most compatible antioxidants in skincare. Works well with Niacinamide, Vitamin C, and Retinol.

blogs.title: How Personal Care Products Make Everyday Life Better
blogs.content:
We Brush Our Teeth Every Day... So Why Not Care for Our Skin?

Most of us never forget to brush our teeth.

We wash our clothes regularly.

We service our vehicles on time.

But when it comes to our skin and hair—the parts of us that face the world every day—we often think,
"I'll use whatever soap is lying around."

The truth is, personal care isn't about looking glamorous.

It's about staying clean, comfortable, healthy, and confident.

A good personal care routine takes less than ten minutes every day, but the benefits can last a lifetime.

Why Personal Care Matters

Think of your skin as your body's protective shield.

Every day it deals with:

  • Dust
  • Pollution
  • Sweat
  • UV rays
  • Bacteria
  • Changing weather
  • Air conditioning

Similarly, your hair and scalp collect oil, dirt and pollution throughout the day.

Using the right products simply helps your body do what it naturally does—protect itself.

Everyday Situations Where Personal Care Makes a Difference

After a Long Day at Work

Imagine reaching home after travelling through traffic in summer.

Your skin feels oily.

Your face looks dull.

A gentle face wash removes dirt, excess oil and pollution, giving your skin a fresh start.

After the Gym

Sweat itself isn't harmful.

But sweat mixed with bacteria can lead to body odour and skin discomfort.

A refreshing shower gel followed by a light moisturiser helps your skin recover faster.

During Winter

Many people blame winter for dry skin.

Actually, hot showers and harsh soaps make it worse.

A moisturising soap, shower gel and body lotion help maintain your skin's natural moisture.

During Monsoon

Humidity often increases oiliness while encouraging bacterial and fungal growth.

Using gentle cleansing products regularly keeps skin fresh without over-drying.

While Travelling

Flights, hotels, changing climates and hard water can stress your skin.

Keeping a simple routine of cleansing, hydrating and moisturising makes travelling much more comfortable.

Personal Care Isn't Vanity—It's Hygiene

People often think skincare is only about beauty.

In reality, it's much more.

Just like washing your hands helps prevent illness, cleansing your skin removes dirt, oil and environmental impurities.

Healthy skin is comfortable skin.

A Simple Everyday Routine TimeWhat to DoMorningCleanse your face, moisturise and use sunscreenDuring BathUse a gentle soap or shower gelHair Wash DaysShampoo and conditionerEveningWash your face and hydrate before sleeping

Consistency matters far more than using dozens of products.

Small Habits, Big Results

Consider these examples.

Rahul, an office executive, started washing his face after returning home instead of waiting until bedtime.

Within a few weeks, his skin looked fresher because pollution wasn't sitting on his face for hours.

Sneha, a teacher, switched from harsh soap to a moisturising bathing bar.

She noticed her skin no longer felt tight after every shower.

Arjun, who regularly visited the gym, started using a shower gel immediately after workouts.

He experienced less body odour and felt fresh throughout the day.

None of these people changed their lives dramatically.

They simply improved one daily habit.

Why Nezal Recommends a Daily Personal Care Routine

Nezal believes skincare should be:

  • Simple enough to follow every day
  • Gentle enough for regular use
  • Effective through consistency
  • Built around carefully selected active ingredients
  • Suitable for modern Indian lifestyles

Good skincare isn't about perfection.

It's about taking small steps every day.

Build Your Routine

☀ Morning

✔ Gentle Face Wash

✔ Aloe Vera Gel or Lightweight Moisturiser

✔ Sunscreen

🚿 Bath Time

✔ Moisturising Soap or Shower Gel

✔ Intimate Wash (Daily)

✔ Shampoo (2–4 times weekly)

🌙 Evening

✔ Face Wash

✔ Hydrating Gel or Serum

✔ Body Lotion

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I really need different personal care products?

Different parts of the body have different needs. Hair, face, body and intimate areas benefit from products formulated specifically for them.

Is a simple routine enough?

Absolutely. Cleansing, hydration and protection are the foundation of healthy skin.

How long before I notice a difference?

Many people notice improved comfort immediately after switching to gentler products. Visible improvements usually appear after several weeks of consistent use.

Can men and women follow the same routine?

Yes. Most personal care principles apply equally to everyone, with only a few product-specific differences.

Friction from clothing and equipment leaves skin tender and reactive. Your post-workout routine needs to do three things fast: cleanse thoroughly without aggravating already-sensitised skin, cool and calm the inflammation that comes with exertion, and restore the moisture balance that intense activity disrupts.
